chapter_seo_title: Chapter 338: "The Collapse" – Dao Gui Yi Xian | A Triple Betrayal
chapter_meta_description: Accused by his own side, Li Huowang faces a three-way attack in the ruins of the Bone Buddha Temple. The Zuowandao’s trap was never a monster, but a poisoned system of trust.
og_title: The Dust Settles on a Frame-Up
og_description: Betrayed from within, Li Huowang is left to fight Master Xinchi, Tuoba Danqing, and Hong Da in the aftermath of a temple collapse.
twitter_title: No monsters, just three friends turning on him.
twitter_description: The “Bone Buddha Temple” hunt goes wrong as Master Xinchi frames Li Huowang for being a Zuowandao impostor, forcing a chaotic three-on-one fight.

lore_anchors.definition: A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office. Their power is both bureaucratic and supernatural, often wielded through a deceptively genial demeanor.
The "Heart-Turbid," one of a class of humanoid treasures similar to Li Huowang's "Heart-Element" (心素). This confirms a hierarchy of rare, sentient ingredients in the Dao-Twisted World.
A Buddhist-derived supernatural power that allows one to see the thoughts of others. In this novel, its acquisition is governed by strict, calculable rules, such as a minimum learning time.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Master Xinchi frame Li Huowang?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is petty and vindictive. He was angered by Li Huowang's earlier defiance and used his position of authority to eliminate Li Huowang by labeling him a false impostor.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the empty cavity in the mummy?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It confirms the Chief Recorder’s secret mission was to retrieve “Xin Zhuo,” a treasure that has already been stolen by the Zuowandao, proving the real loot was never the trap.
